item.title: Pat Murphy takes brutal shot at Yankees while celebrating Brewers’ World Series Title with Jake Bauers
item.description: Pat Murphy guided the Milwaukee Brewers to their first World Series title, sealing the championship with a five-game win over the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday. Jake Bauers, who is approaching free agency, made valuable contributions throughout Milwaukee’s season. A postgame exchange between Murphy and Bauers caught attention, particularly after the manager delivered a pointed remark about the New York Yankees. Spectrum News 1 Wisconsin shared the moment. Jake Bauers gives Pat Murphy the last out ball. #Brewers #WorldSeries #WinOurWay #ThisIsMyCrew pic.twitter.com/E3pblrbzf8 — Spectrum News 1 Wisconsin (@SpectrumNews1WI) October 29, 2026 “Just remember, when you’re on that horses**t Yankees team and you guys are all playing for yourselves, just remember this is the way we used to do it,” the Brewers manager told Bauers. Jake Bauers with Pat Murphy and the Brewers Sep 20, 2025; St. Louis, Missouri, USA; Milwaukee Brewers left fielder Bauers (9) is congratulated by manager Pat Murphy (49) after scoring against the St. Louis Cardinals during the second inning at Busch Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Curry-Imagn Images Players who establish their value with smaller-market clubs often attract lucrative offers from larger franchises once they reach free agency. Bauers may soon find himself in that position, with the Yankees potentially among his suitors. Should New York pursue him, Murphy’s remarks after the Brewers’ championship celebration could make the first baseman reconsider whether joining the Bronx club is the right move. Sep 20, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy looks on prior to the game between the Baltimore Orioles and the Milwaukee Brewers Oriole Park at Camden Yards. Mandatory Credit: James A. Pittman-Imagn Images Bauers put together a strong regular season, batting .266 with an .874 OPS and 26 homers. He carried that production into the playoffs, e arning NLCS MVP honors followed by an inconsistent showing in the World Series. His performance across the season has given the left-handed hitter a strong case to test the free-agent market and pursue a sizable deal. After playing such a key role in Milwaukee’s championship run, Bauers could remain part of the Brewers’ plans. Whether the team will make a serious effort to bring him back is now one of the questions surrounding his upcoming free agency. item.title: Staples girls basketball coach arrested after police say he choked referee during game over foul call
item.description: Thomas Sparks was arrested after police say he choked a basketball referee during a youth game in Shelton on Oct. 24, 2026. (Courtesy of Shelton Police Department ) The Staples High School girls basketball coach has resigned after being arrested for allegedly tripping and choking a referee over a disputed call during a youth game in Shelton last week, officials said. Thomas Sparks, 37, was arrested Oct. 24 and charged with third-degree assault, second-degree strangulation and risk of injury to a child after a referee at a youth basketball game at the Boys and Girls Club in Shelton filed a complaint, a police report said. Sparks resigned Thursday as Staples girls basketball coach. "Tommy resigned for personal and family considerations," Staples High School Athletic Director said in a text message on Friday. Sparks was coaching a team for the Connecticut Elite youth basketball league on Oct. 24 when he confronted the referee about what he perceived to be a bad foul call, the police report said. Officials at Connecticut Elite declined to discuss the incident on Friday, but said Sparks no longer worked for them. During a verbal exchange, the referee told police Sparks called him a "dickhead," and then seconds later tripped and shoved him to the ground, according to the report. Before the referee could get up, Sparks put his arm around the man's neck at which point others in the crowd stepped in to intervene, the police report said. Sparks was ejected from the building and the referee later showed up at the police station to file a report. He told police that he felt like he might pass out while Sparks had his arm was around his neck, the report said. Sparks told police that he took physical action because he didn't know what the referee would do after their verbal exchange, the report said. Witnesses, including some of the players, confirmed the referee's version of events, police said. Sparks was released on $10,000 bond and is due back in court Nov. 12. item.title: UCLA QB Nico Iamaleava Makes Major 2027 NFL Draft Decision After Season-Ending ACL Injury
item.description: UCLA Bruins has received clarity on its quarterback plans after Nico Iamaleava decided to remain with the program. His return follows a shortened 2026 campaign that ended with a knee injury. Iamaleava’s decision comes after helping the Bruins win their first five games. His agent confirmed the decision, and the quarterback later addressed his future in an Instagram post. UCLA QB plans to remain with the Bruins UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava plans to return to the Bruins for the 2027 season instead of entering the 2027 NFL Draft. His agent confirmed the decision to On3 reporter Pete Nakos. Iamaleava will return to UCLA after a torn ACL ended his 2026 season. Oct 10, 2026; Eugene, Oregon, USA; UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava (9) drops back for a pass during the first quarter against the Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images The announcement read: “NEW: UCLA QB Nico Iamaleava has informed the Bruins he plans to return next season, his agent tells @PeteNakos ” Iamaleava previously played two seasons with the Tennessee Volunteers before joining UCLA in 2025. He became the Bruins’ starting quarterback and recorded 1,928 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions in his first season with the program. He started the 2026 season with five consecutive wins. In those games, Iamaleava completed 72 of 116 passes for 982 yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions. He also recorded 144 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown as UCLA improved to 5-0. His season ended on October 10 against Oregon after he suffered a torn ACL. He left the game and was ruled out for the remainder of the 2026 season. Ty Dieffenbach took over at quarterback following Iamaleava’s injury. He helped UCLA secure a 17-15 victory over Oregon before leading the team to wins against Wisconsin and Michigan State. Across those three games, Dieffenbach recorded 505 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception. UCLA improved to 7-0 following those three victories. After the injury, Iamaleava addressed his season-ending setback in an Instagram post. He expressed his disappointment and shared his plans to return to football. He wrote : “Well, I’m heartbroken the way my season ended. I’ve finally accepted that this year is really over for me. This wasn’t a part of the plan, but I believe everything happens for a reason. I gave this game and my brothers everything I had and I’ll continue to lean on God and trust His plan. I’ll be back.” The confirmation followed Iamaleava’s social media message after the injury. Iamaleava will rejoin UCLA’s quarterback competition alongside Dieffenbach, who also has remaining college eligibility. Dieffenbach’s performances during Iamaleava’s absence have given the Bruins another option at the position. Both quarterbacks remain part of UCLA’s plans entering the 2027 season. item.title: Jeffery Simmons’ Arrival Has Experts High on Bears’ Super Bowl Chances
item.description: The Chicago Bears acquired defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans. The trade gives Chicago a star defender ahead of the deadline. ESPN analyst Field Yates praised the move. He noted that adding Jeffery Simmons immediately makes the Chicago Bears serious Super Bowl contenders. Bears’ blockbuster move for Jeffery Simmons fuels championship talk The Bears sent 2027 and 2028 first-round picks to Tennessee. They also included a 2027 fourth-round pick. Chicago received Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The trade fills a major need for Chicago. It gives the team a proven leader on the defensive line. This helps their playoff push. Dec 7, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (98) reacts after sacking Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders (not pictured) during the fourth quarter at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Scott Galvin-Imagn Images Field Yates stated , “The Bears look like a team good enough to be hoisting a Lombardi trophy.” Simmons is coming off his first first-team All-Pro season in 2025. He had a career-high 11 sacks that year. Simmons remained a dominant force on the interior defensive line this season, consistently disrupting opposing backfields before the trade. Simmons spent his entire career with the Titans until this trade. He is 29 years old and was selected 19th overall by the Titans in the 2019 NFL Draft. The move gives Chicago a proven interior defender. Entering the 2026 NFL season, the defensive tackle was playing under a three-year, $105.8 million contract extension with $100 million guaranteed, averaging $35.27 million per year. The Bears will take on that contract as they pursue a Super Bowl run. The front office has officially signaled an all-in approach for the current campaign . Tennessee received two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick. The deal gives the Titans draft capital for a rebuild. Simmons fills a major need for Chicago’s interior pass rush, which has struggled to generate consistent pressure from the defensive tackles this season. His arrival immediately upgrades the front seven. Titans general manager Ran Carthon said Simmons was an elite player on and off the field. The Titans announced the trade Thursday, and the Bears made it official shortly after. The Bears had been noted as a potential aggressive buyer before the deadline. Chicago previously acquired pass rusher Montez Sweat in a similar midseason trade during the 2023 season. The front office has signaled an all-in approach for the current campaign. item.title: Hornets’ 25 Turnovers Killed Game Against Pistons On Wednesday
item.description: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets need to fix their ball-handling issues immediately. The loss to the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday night showed exactly what happens when the team turns the ball over too much. Cade Cunningham scored 30 points to lead Detroit to a 97-89 win. The Hornets simply could not stop the bleeding with their mistakes. It was a tough night for a young squad that needs to learn how to protect the rock. Turnovers Cost Charlotte Everything The numbers tell a clear story about why the Hornets lost. Charlotte turned the ball over 25 times while Detroit only had 14. That is a huge gap that no team can overcome easily. The Pistons forced eight turnovers in the third quarter alone. This surge helped Detroit start the period with a 16-5 run. The Hornets had built a lead earlier but could not hold it. The lack of ball security was the main reason the game slipped away. Brandon Miller tried to keep the team in the hunt. He finished with 31 points and 12 rebounds for Charlotte. But his shooting struggles in the final period hurt the chances of a comeback. In the fourth quarter, Miller missed five out of his seven shots. Dennis Schroeder added 14 points but no other player reached double figures. The team needs more scoring depth if they want to win close games. Second Quarter Struggles Defined the Loss Charlotte looked good in the first half. The Hornets held a 51-44 lead at the break thanks to Miller’s 21 points. Neither team could hit shots consistently during the game. The Hornets did manage to grab six more second-chance points than Detroit. That small edge kept them ahead for a while. But the Pistons started the third quarter with a massive run that changed the flow. Four different Detroit players hit 3-pointers during that stretch. The Pistons are now 4-1 on the season. They came off a big loss to New York on Tuesday but bounced back quickly. The Hornets need to figure out how to stop these runs. A team cannot win if they give up easy baskets and turn the ball over repeatedly. The loss to Detroit on Wednesday night is a clear warning. The young players must learn to handle the pressure better. The Hornets will need to fix their defense and ball movement fast. The Pistons showed that they can score from anywhere on the floor. Charlotte cannot afford to play this sloppy again. The team must cut down on those 25 turnovers in the next game.

item.title: Lake Norman volleyball player shares bond with coach through cancer battle
item.description: One Huntersville high school is celebrating its champions -- Lake Norman Charter High School’s varsity volleyball team just took the state title for the second year in a row on Friday. Channel 9’s Elsa Gillis met with the team before their championship game and learned the team is no stranger to fighting tough battles on and off the court. “Oh my gosh! So I’ve known Coach Zoey ... she’s awesome,” Avery Caruso told Channel 9. Avery Caruso lights up when she talks about her volleyball coach, Zoey Reid. “She always helps like inspire us when we’re in our huddles. She always knows what to say,” Avery said. The feeling is mutual. “I like to call it a God-winked moment that I got to coach Avery,” Zoey said. Avery is a freshman, but plays varsity volleyball at Lake Norman Charter High School. She and her assistant coach share an unlikely bond off the court. “I remember basically everything, so it was really hard,” Avery said. Avery is a childhood cancer survivor. She was diagnosed with leukemia at age 9. She’s now in remission and celebrating a big milestone. “Today is the day that I rang the bell four years ago,” Avery said. But Coach Zoey is in the thick of her own battle. “My senior year of college, I was diagnosed with stage four rhabdomyosarcoma, which is a soft tissue muscle cancer, and it’s very, very, very rare,” Zoey said. She overcame it once. But last summer, she relapsed, just after getting the job as the head middle school and assistant varsity coach. “I’m like, wait, I can’t go through all this intensive treatment. I’ve literally just got this job, and I’m coaching these little girls, and they need me,” Zoey said. But through the treatment, she continues to show up. “She’s such a fighter,” Avery said. As they do for her. “If I couldn’t speak because I was doing treatment that day, or if I couldn’t coach or I couldn’t go out there and give it my all, those girls didn’t mind. They were still there in my corner no matter what, making sure. ‘Hey, coach, do you need a fan or do you need some water?’” Zoey said. “It’s, I get to go to volleyball today. I don’t ‘have,’ it’s not ‘have.’ It’s like I ‘get’ to, because there’s somebody laying in a hospital bed right now, wishing they had the opportunity that I had to just wake up and walk and go to school and go and teach or do anything,” Zoey said. Together, they’re learning what it really takes to be a champion on and off the court.

item.title: Dak Prescott Issues Blunt Mandate to Cowboys Squad Following 3-4 Start to Season
item.description: Dak Prescott has put the Dallas Cowboys on notice after a rough start at home. The Cowboys are 3-4 after losing three of four games at AT&T Stadium. Prescott urged his teammates to protect home turf ahead of the Arizona Cardinals game. Dallas found balance in a win over Philadelphia, rushing for 204 yards. The team also produced more than 200 passing yards. Prescott now wants that level of play to continue at home. Dak Prescott sets high standards for Cowboys squad Prescott’s message followed a 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas struggled to stop the run in that game. Bucky Irving finished with 165 rushing yards, including a 72-yard run to open the second half. Oct 26, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) calls a playb during the fourth quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images “Even more so important to come back and come back home and to get a win after the last time being here at home. And yeah, you’ve got to win your games at home. That’s a huge advantage,” Prescott said . The loss was compounded by self-inflicted mistakes, including missed tackles, explosive plays allowed, and a costly kickoff fumble by KaVontae Turpin. That turnover helped Tampa Bay create a 14-point advantage. Jerry Jones called the performance “extraordinarily, extraordinarily disappointing,” a frustration heightened by the Buccaneers entering the matchup winless. Prescott echoed that sentiment, clarifying that Dallas simply failed to control a game they were fully expected to win. Arizona presents a different challenge despite its 2-5 record. The Cardinals have consistently caused problems for Dallas in recent seasons, including a tough 28-16 loss in Arizona last year. They enter this matchup having won all four of their previous games at AT&T Stadium. Their recent record against the Cowboys makes it difficult to treat this as a routine home game. Dallas will also need to prove that the improvement against Philadelphia was more than a one-week response. The Cowboys had scored only 29 points across the two games before the Eagles matchup. Against Arizona, they must maintain their commitment to the running game while protecting Prescott from pressure. The Cardinals are expected to test Dallas with more blitz looks, an area that caused problems for the Cowboys earlier in the season. Prescott said the offense has prepared for those situations, but the adjustments will have to work under game pressure. For Dallas, the formula is straightforward. The Cowboys must run the ball efficiently and avoid turnovers. They must also prevent Arizona from producing explosive plays. A win would move the Cowboys to 4-4 and give them their first back-to-back victories of the season. Another home loss, however, would raise serious questions about their ability to compete consistently in the NFC East. More NFL News Los Angeles Rams Announce Matthew Stafford Milestone

Here, the situation became even more complicated. In June, when the FHSAA formally approved the Open Division, the association listed its primary three-team tiebreaker as points allowed among tied teams only . This was the same tiebreaker the FHSAA installed for other team sports such as basketball and soccer, but its use in volleyball drew criticism from multiple coaches. Applied to volleyball, the provision in effect made a loss by three-set sweep more advantageous than a five-set battle to the finish. In response to these questions, an Oct. 26 letter from FHSAA administrator Scott Jamison said, the association intended to "look at the average points allowed per set for sets 1-4 amongst the tied teams." A day later, the proposed tiebreaker appeared to change again. An Oct. 27 e-mail from the FHSAA, received by the Beachside athletic department, said the association would now designate its tiebreaker as the set winning percentage within the Open Division matches. During these discussions, however, the FHSAA's website did not remove the points allowed from its listing of primary tiebreakers. The FHSAA board of directors, due to hold its next meeting Nov. 1-2 in Gainesville, also took no action. Set percentage is a widely accepted standard method of breaking a three-team tie in volleyball, used by USA Volleyball , the California Interscholastic Federation and some college conferences . However, rather than applying the set percentage all the way across the tied teams, the FHSAA would apply the tiebreaker only to determine the first-place finisher in the three-team tie. Once the FHSAA identified the highest-placed team on set percentage, the association would use head-to-head between the two remaining teams to choose the second-place finisher. What was the new tiebreaker's result? Based on the set percentage tiebreaker, Calvary Christian placed first, winning 8 of its 12 sets (2-3 loss to Beachside, 3-0 win over First Baptist, 3-1 win over Plant). That earned the Clearwater school the top spot in Pool B. Had the FHSAA applied set percentage to each position in the group, Beachside would have held the edge. Beachside won 8 of 14 sets for a .571 percentage (3-2 win over Calvary Christian, 3-2 loss to Plant, 3-1 win over First Baptist), while Plant won 7 of 13, or .538 (3-1 win over First Baptist, 3-2 win over Beachside, 3-1 loss to Calvary Christian). But because the FHSAA used head-to-head ranking as its second tiebreaker, Plant advanced to the knockout stage, because of its victory over Beachside on Oct. 24. What happens next for Beachside? For Beachside (26-4), whose season came to a close despite defeating First Baptist in four sets on Oct. 28, the exit has sparked anger, frustration and bewilderment, even as the team also celebrates its most successful season in history. As Beachside athletic director Jen Harman noted, the two-step tiebreaker formula could create bizarre incentives. Although Plant did not do this, the Tampa school theoretically could have qualified automatically by committing 75 consecutive faults for a 25-0, 25-0, 25-0 loss, which would have given Calvary Christian an automatic first place while securing second place for Plant due to their prior head-to-head result over Beachside. But if Plant lost to Calvary Christian in five, the Tampa school potentially could have suffered elimination. Beachside head coach Austin Lanteigne said he doesn't want the tiebreaker hubbub to detract from the Barracudas' achievements. "If you would have told our girls in June that we would go 2-1 in the Open Division, we would have been happy," Lanteigne said after Wednesday's match. Unfortunately for the Barracudas, 2-1 in the Open Division wasn't enough to clear the tiebreaker. Wednesday's home victory ended the high school careers for six Beachside senior standouts: Vinessa Rafael, Isabella Taveras Seda, Mollie VanDeusen, Lillian Jimenez, Leanna Deutou and Maya Bell. The senior class compiled a record of 93-18 during the past four years. It's not immediately clear whether the FHSAA will revisit its tiebreaking procedure for the 2027 volleyball season. item.title: NBA Fans Are Asking Questions After Naz Reid Gets Shockingly Benched by Hornets
item.description: Photo by: Lon Horwedel The Charlotte Hornets made a surprising decision Wednesday night, and it has quickly become one of the biggest talking points surrounding the team. Naz Reid, one of Charlotte’s biggest offseason additions, was unexpectedly benched for the entire second half of the team’s 97-89 loss to the Detroit Pistons. What makes the situation even more interesting is that Reid wasn’t dealing with an injury. Instead, head coach Charles Lee decided he had seen enough during the first half and kept the veteran forward on the bench for the remainder of the game. What Happened Between Reid and the Coaching Staff? Reid finished the first half with seven points, six rebounds and one block in 13 minutes. However, something apparently happened that led Lee to make the surprising decision. After the game, Lee addressed the situation but didn’t provide many details. “Unfortunately, Naz didn’t meet our standards in the first half,” Lee explained. He added that the team made the decision at halftime that Reid would not play again. The coach did not clarify exactly which standards Reid failed to meet, leaving fans searching for answers. Footage from the first half also raised questions. Reid appeared to have a confusing exchange involving offensive play signals before a sequence that ended with another difficult possession. Some observers have speculated that communication and execution may have played a role, but the exact reason remains unconfirmed. A Strange Decision That Cost Charlotte The timing made the decision even more surprising. Charlotte actually entered halftime leading Detroit 51-44, but the Pistons completely took control after the break. Detroit outscored the Hornets 53-38 in the second half, eventually securing an eight-point victory. Reid had been playing well to begin his Charlotte career, averaging 19.5 points and 9.5 rebounds through his first four games. What Happens Next? The good news for Charlotte fans is that reports indicate Reid and Lee cleared the air following the game. Reid is expected to move forward with the team rather than allowing the situation to become a bigger distraction. Still, benching one of your most important players for an entire half is a major statement. Was Lee sending a message, or is there more to this situation than fans know?

The good news for Charlotte fans is that reports indicate Reid and Lee cleared the air following the game. item.title: Leclerc fastest in Mexico City Grand Prix first practice
item.description: Charles Leclerc went fastest in a practice session featuring 10 rookie drivers [Reuters] Ferrari's Charles Leclerc led Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli in first practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix, where the Italian is poised to clinch his first world title. Leclerc was 0.659 seconds quicker than Antonelli, for whom a ninth-place finish will secure the championship regardless of any other results. Only a victory by his team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can theoretically stop Antonelli becoming champion on Sunday. Even then, Antonelli only needs ninth place if Russell wins and 10th if Hamilton does. Third quickest in the session was Mercedes reserve Frederik Vesti, driving Russell's car, ahead of Hamilton. Mercedes were one of 10 teams to choose this session to do one of their mandatory rookie sessions. Only Ferrari had both race drivers in their cars. Mexico City is chosen by many teams to run their mandatory rookie sessions because the first session is traditionally unrepresentative as a result of the dirty track surface. Japanese Ayumu Iwasa, in for Max Verstappen at Red Bull, was fifth fastest, ahead of Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso. McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Haas driver Oliver Bearman and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10. Briton Freddie Slater's first outing at a grand prix weekend for Audi did not go to plan. Reliability problems limited his running to 14 laps - about half a standard mileage. But he did manage to get out for the final 20 minutes or so and set the 19th fastest time. He was just behind another Briton, Luke Browning having his latest run in the Williams. American Colton Herta, who Cadillac are considering promoting to F1 next year in place of Valtteri Bottas, was 22nd. Governing body the FIA says Herta, a nine-time winner in Indycar, has now done enough miles to score the 40 points he needs to secure the superlicence required to race in F1. item.title: Hugo González, Baylor Scheierman extend tenure with Boston Celtics
item.description: Saturday, Oct. 31, marked an important day for Boston Celtics wings Baylor Scheierman and Hugo González. It was the deadline for the Green Team to make a decision on the club options for the aforementioned C's. There was no spooky contract drama on Halloween night, though, as the Celtics picked up both 2027-28 rookie scale options on Friday afternoon, per Keith Smith of Spotrac . These two moves will fully guarantee Scheierman and González's money for next season and, barring a trade or another unforeseen maneuver, keep them in the green and white until 2028 at the very least. Following the 2027-28 campaign, González will encounter a club option once again while Scheierman will become a restricted free agent — unless he's extended next summer. Boston's backup wings have put together a relatively slow start to the season. González logged 0 points in his first two outings before scorching the Chicago Bulls on Monday night with 13 points on almost 67 percent shooting during a 134-99 victory. Scheierman has been even quieter. He's yet to score in double figures but has averaged a little over 17 minutes per game thus far. Through four contests, the Celtics hold a 3-1 record and hover around the top of the Eastern Conference standings. They could tie the 4-1 Detroit Pistons and 4-1 Philadelphia 76ers with a win on Friday night versus the Bulls at TD Garden. Although 26-year-old Scheierman and 20-year-old González haven't wowed to open up the regular season, they provide the Celtics with crucial depth and should be called upon more in November. item.description: A pile of footballs sit before a high school football game in South Bend, Ind. item.title: FIA hands out first grid penalty of the weekend in Mexico City
item.description: Cadillac 's Valtteri Bottas is set to start the Mexico City Grand Prix from the back of the grid on Sunday afternoon. The first grid penalty has already been handed out at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Several power unit components have been changed in the Finnish driver's Cadillac, including the internal combustion engine, turbocharger, energy store, control electronics unit and MGU-K. These component changes add up to a 50-place grid penalty for the Finn, which means he will start Sunday's race from the back of the grid. Bottas is yet complete a single lap today as of now. During the first free practice session, he handed over his car to Colton Herta. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Leclerc and Ferrari set the pace in FP1 in Mexico City Charles Leclerc topped the opening session of the weekend in Mexico. The Monegasque driver finished ahead of Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and Frederik Vesti. Moreover, his lap time was around two tenths of a second quicker than the fastest time recorded in FP1 during the 2025 season. However, the final results are not the most representative in terms of the pecking order this weekend, as Max Verstappen, Lando Norris and George Russell, among others, did not participate in the session. Audi under investigation by the FIA stewards Stewards have also launched their first investigation of the Grand Prix weekend after Audi sent Freddie Slater out onto the track with a fan still attached to his car. A team representative was summoned to appear before the stewards at 14:00 local time (20:00 UK time).

item.title: Jack Nicklaus predicted Bryson DeChambeau would pull off never seen before feat during the 2020 Masters
item.description: Photo by Sam Greenwood/Getty Images Jack Nicklaus is not one for hyperbole. So the prediction he made about Bryson DeChambeau back in 2020 really did raise some eyebrows. Nicklaus is the greatest golfer of all time, certainly if we take major wins as the main barometer. The Golden Bear won 18 major championships throughout his career, including six wins at The Masters. Jack Nicklaus knows Augusta National like the back of his hand, and his knowledge of the golf course played a key role in his record of six Masters titles. Meanwhile, Bryson DeChambeau has won two majors, although he is still yet to earn himself a green jacket. With his skillset, he will surely win The Masters one day. His length off the tee and shot shape from right to left make his game tailor-made for Augusta National. Speaking of his prodigious speed and power, Nicklaus believed that the LIV Golf star’s length off the tee would enable him to overpower Augusta back in 2020. The prediction Jack Nicklaus made about Bryson DeChambeau in 2020 Nicklaus spoke to Golf.com about DeChambeau ahead of The Masters in 2020. Due to Covid, The Masters was not played until November of that year, and due to the firm and fast conditions, the Golden Bear made a truly jaw-dropping prediction about the LIV golfer. “Well, let’s start off what he could do, “ Nicklaus began. “He could drive the 1st green. If it’s firm, he could drive the 1st green. Under the right conditions. “ It’s worth pointing out here that the first hole at Augusta National is 455 yards, and it is uphill! Now, players can slightly cut the corner on the first hole, and by doing so, shorten the hole by perhaps 40 yards. Still, in order for Bryson DeChambeau to drive the green on the first hole at Augusta National, he would need a wind bordering on a gale at his back. While DeChambeau is the longest hitter in the game, he will almost certainly never drive the green on the opening hole at The Masters. Nicklaus’ prediction about the two-time US Open winner has to go down as one of his poorer ones throughout the years.

item.title: Novak Djokovic’s ATP Finals chances handed huge blow as the Paris Masters draw is revealed
item.description: Novak Djokovic suffered a shock early exit from the Basel Open this week, and in the process suffered a huge blow to his chances of qualifying for the ATP Finals. The only consolation was that Rafael Jodar, his biggest competitor for that final spot, also lost. The fight was still on. However, that still hinged massively on the 39-year-old putting together a strong run of form through two consecutive events, one of which he had not played at in 15 years. Now, Novak Djokovic needs to achieve something exceptional in the French capital to even stand a chance. Unfortunately for him, luck has once again not been on his side. Novak Djokovic’s nightmare Paris Masters draw As if things could get no harder for Djokovic, he will be forced to kickstart his campaign in Paris against the dangerously in-form Valentin Vacherot. Last year’s Shanghai Masters champion is coming off the back of a semi-final run in Japan, and will play Taylor Fritz tomorrow for a spot in the Basel Open final. Clearly, on indoor courts, the Monegasque player is a threat. If Djokovic can bypass Vacherot, he will be afforded some reprieve in the second round, facing either Luciano Darderi or a qualifier. However, this is when the gauntlet really starts. One of Alex de Minaur or Andrey Rublev should await in the third round, before Alexander Zverev, the top seed and newly-crowned world number one, stands out in his quarter. To beat the German would take an almighty feat, though he did manage it just a few weeks ago. Sadly, Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe or Tommy Paul all could be his semi-final opponents. Finalists could range from Carlos Alcaraz to Daniil Medvedev, or even Arthur Fils. It is a truly nightmarish run. How can Novak Djokovic qualify for the ATP Finals now? With his performances in Basel, Medvedev has already secured his spot at the ATP Finals . That leaves just four remaining. The bare minimum Djokovic needs to stay in contention is a semi-final, but that only works if rivals like De Minaur and Fritz gain no more points this week and lose their Paris openers. Winning would take the 39-year-old to 3,890 and past Jodar, which should secure his place. However, if De Minaur wins Vienna this week and then reaches the Paris final, he’d reach 3,930 and narrowly edge out even a title-winning Djokovic. His only last-minute course of action would then be to enter the ATP 250 event in Stockholm.

item.title: Porro, Gallagher And Solanke To Start | 4-2-3-1 Tottenham Hotspur Predicted Lineup Vs Crystal Palace
item.description: Porro, Gallagher And Solanke To Start | 4-2-3-1 Tottenham Hotspur Predicted Lineup Vs Crystal Palace Tottenham Hotspur will entertain Crystal Palace at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this Saturday evening as they look to secure all three points at home in the London derby. Spurs managed to secure a solid 2-0 win away at Chelsea recently, which should give them a ton of confidence going into this game. Roberto De Zerbi will set his men up in a 4-2-3-1 formation and is expected to make a few changes to his first team for this clash. Pedro Porro, Conor Gallagher and Dominic Solanke could all play from the start of this game. 4-2-3-1 Tottenham Hotspur Predicted Lineup To Face Crystal Palace Defence Antonin Kinsky will feature in between the sticks for Tottenham after keeping a clean sheet in his last appearance. Micky van de Ven will operate alongside Jan Paul van Hecke at the centre of De Zerbi’s defence as they look to keep a good shape on the defensive end of the field. Pedro Porro will try to catch the eye as the right-back, while Andy Robertson looks to give a good account of himself on the other side as the left-back. Both of them will get the license to go forward and express themselves inside the Palace half. Ben Davies will offer cover for the defensive positions on the bench. item.title: Hansi Flick agrees with Barcelona star Rodri’s post-Real Madrid defeat assessment
item.description: Hansi Flick agrees with Barcelona star Rodri’s post-Real Madrid defeat assessment Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has admitted that he is in agreement with midfield star Rodri, regarding the needs of the Blaugrana’s squad when in difficult situations on the pitch. Barcelona are of course fresh off an altogether disappointing last week on the results front. After rattling off 11 consecutive victories to open the campaign, the Blaugrana were condemned to back-to-back defeats at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid. item.title: Fabrizio Romano confirmation sets scene for Liverpool, timeline to sign genius player
item.description: Fabrizio Romano confirmation sets scene for Liverpool, timeline to sign genius player Fabrizio Romano has laid out the timeline and now Liverpool know what they've got to do. A truly genius player will be on the market. Liverpool have made a habit of signing the best-possible talents in world football over the last couple of summers. That thinking has seen them spend over nine figures on three different players, having never come particularly close to spending that before. But it's the new strategy. Sign the best players available and then find a way to build a functioning team out of them. While that last bit has been a struggle up to now, there's a lot of faith in Andoni Iraola to figure it all out. It also means that Liverpool will once again look for a big name in 2027. We do expect major signings in midfield and at centre-back but that doesn't mean the attack is completely sorted. In fact, there is room for another big arrival next year, especially after the Reds tried to sell Cody Gakpo at the end of the transfer window. Couple that with a need for some sort of left-footed attacker and we think the chance is there for arguably the most exciting signing of all. Nico Paz up for grabs Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that Nico Paz will not move in January. Instead, it's expected that there will be a battle for his signature next summer when Real Madrid have a buyback clause. This is the second buyback clause they've had for Paz. The first was activated last summer, only for Los Blancos to immediately sell him back to Como with an increased one. Como, then, know they can't control his future beyond next summer. They have no intention of changing that and will refuse any January offers on account of his form this season and importance to the team. Paz is quite clearly one of the biggest prospects in football right now. He was outstanding last season and looks improved in this campaign - a genuinely sensational talent who can seemingly do it all. We've written recently about just how good Paz is and just how much of an impact he could have on Liverpool's attack. He's the kind of player that everyone should try to sign. It's exactly the situation that the Reds current strategy calls for, in fact. One in which you sign the best available player and then look to make it work. Paz is exactly that: the best player available. With the caveat that Real Madrid could ultimately look to integrate him. We feel that's a little unlikely given the wealth of attacking midfield options they already boast - it would be difficult to guarantee him a starting XI role from the get go. Liverpool could. And should.

item.title: Knueppel’s G League Move Signals Hornets Return Is Close
item.description: Mike Watters-Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets finally have a clear sign that Kon Knueppel is ready to play. The team sent the forward to the Greensboro Swarm for a practice session on Thursday. This move means the 21-year-old is getting his legs back under him after missing the first five games. He was injured during offseason work, and fans have been waiting to see him shoot in a real game. The team confirmed the assignment in a post on X, stating, “OFFICIAL: @hornets have assigned forward Kon Knueppel to the @greensboroswarm for today’s practice.” It is a huge step forward for a player who led the league in three-pointers last year. The Path Back From Injury Knueppel missed the entire preseason and the start of this season due to a strained left hamstring. He suffered the injury just over a month ago. Now, he is using the G League to build up his stamina without the pressure of a full NBA game. These assignments are standard for players recovering from soft tissue issues. Basketnews.com wrote on the team’s decision, “This move is part of his rehabilitation process. Assignments to a G League affiliate for practice are commonly used to give recovering players additional on-court work.” The Hornets need his scoring punch badly. Brandon Miller is averaging 25.6 points per game, but he cannot carry the load alone forever. No Date Set Yet The team has not set a specific date for his return. Head coach Charles Lee spoke at a press conference and admitted they still do not have a plan. “No timeline, as far as I know right now,” the Hornets coach said. He added, “I hope that during this road trip, or after the road trip, we’ll get a little bit more information.” The team is playing the Washington Wizards on Friday and the Philadelphia 76ers on Saturday. Lee might wait until after this trip to make a call. Some reports from ESPN’s injury report suggest a return date of November 2, but that is just a guess until the coach confirms it. The Hornets need Knueppel to help them compete in the Eastern Conference. Last season, he finished second in Rookie of the Year voting after averaging 18.5 points. Without him, the team has won three of five games despite losing to the Pistons on Wednesday. The loss to Detroit showed how much the team struggles without their top shooter. Naz Reid was benched for not meeting standards, and the offense stalled. The team traded LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, so they need the young talent to step up. If he practices well on Thursday, he could be ready for the Pistons game on Monday.

item.title: ¡MALAGÓN MANDA MENSAJE TRAS LA MALA RACHA EN EL AZTECA!
item.description: ¡MALAGÓN MANDA MENSAJE TRAS LA MALA RACHA EN EL AZTECA! El guardameta del América reconoció que el equipo atraviesa una racha de cinco partidos sin ganar; sin embargo, aseguró que el grupo mantiene la tranquilidad El Club América atraviesa un momento en el que los resultados no han acompañado al equipo como esperaba su afición. Son cinco partidos sin conocer la victoria, una situación que representa un desafío para una institución acostumbrada a competir por los primeros lugares. Sin embargo, dentro del vestidor azulcrema mantienen la confianza en que el panorama puede cambiar. Durante la conferencia de prensa previa al encuentro frente a Toluca, Luis Ángel Malagón habló sobre la actualidad del conjunto americanista y dejó claro que, pese a la racha negativa, el equipo no pierde de vista sus objetivos. “Son cinco partidos de no ganar, pero todo es parte de… al final seguimos en la parte alta y mañana será un rival más”, expresó el arquero azulcrema. CONFIANZA TOTAL EN AMÉRICA Las palabras de Malagón reflejan la postura de un equipo que busca mantener la calma en medio de la exigencia que representa defender los colores del América. El guardameta reconoció implícitamente que los resultados recientes no han sido los esperados, pero también puso sobre la mesa un aspecto importante: el conjunto continúa ubicado en la parte alta de la clasificación. Te recomiendo AMÉRICA DEJA ESCAPAR EL TRIUNFO ANTE XOLOS El compromiso ante Toluca representa una nueva oportunidad para que las Águilas puedan reencontrarse con la victoria y comenzar a dejar atrás esta racha. No será un encuentro sencillo, pues enfrente tendrán a un rival que también llega con aspiraciones importantes dentro del campeonato. Para Malagón, el mensaje es claro: mantener la tranquilidad, trabajar y afrontar cada partido con la responsabilidad que exige representar al americanismo.

item.title: Chad Kelly’s Historic CFL Deal Proves NFL Wrong
item.description: Nov 9, 2024; Montreal, Quebec, CAN; Toronto Argonauts quarterback Chad Kelly (12) passes the ball against the Montreal Alouettes during the first quarter at Percival-Molson Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images His new contract makes Chad Kelly the first million-dollar player in the league’s salary cap era. The NFL passed on him, but the CFL is now paying him like a franchise cornerstone. According to multiple reports, including figures cited by the New York Post , the deal could reach $5,805,250, including bonuses. That is real money for a man the NFL labeled Mr. Irrelevant. The numbers tell the story of a player who found his footing after being discarded. Before this extension, BC Lions quarterback Nathan Rourke held the title of highest-paid player with a salary of $684,700. Kelly’s new deal dwarfs that figure and changes the economic landscape for every quarterback in Canada. He posted career highs this season with 5,067 passing yards and 33 touchdowns. Those stats are not just good; they are elite by any standard. A Home in Toronto Kelly did not just sign a check; he found a place to stay. During a press conference on Tuesday, he said coming to the CFL “was the best decision I ever made in my life.” He added that he has a beautiful family and has “come to love Canada on a whole other level.” He stated that he “never knew I could come to love a place so much (more) than my home and now this is my home forever,” and that he is “just thankful to be in this situation.” This sentiment matters because it shows he is not just passing through. He helped the Argonauts win the Grey Cup in 2022 and has been a key part of their offense since. The NFL treated him as a bust after taking him last overall in the 2017 draft. He never found his footing there. Now he is the face of the league in Canada with a contract that secures his future. The Cost of Being Mr. Irrelevant The NFL draft is a cruel machine that often throws away talent . Kelly was the last pick in 2017. He is the nephew of Buffalo Bills great Jim Kelly, which makes the NFL’s rejection even more striking. He spent years bouncing around before finding success in the CFL. The league that ignored him is now watching from the sidelines while he signs a historic extension. Although the Argonauts did not release financial terms after the official announcement, the reported figures are clear. This deal proves that a player can rebuild a career if given the chance. Kelly set new records this year, and the team rewarded him accordingly. The gap between his NFL draft status and his current value is massive. He is no longer a question mark. He is the highest-paid player in the league and a proven winner. The NFL missed out on a quarterback who can throw for over 5,000 yards and lead a team to a championship. That is a mistake the league will have to live with. Kelly is settled in Toronto and ready to play for years to come.

item.title: Arteta can take inspiration from George Graham to expunge painful Anfield memories
item.description: Arsenal have not won at Liverpool for 13 league games but Gunners’ win in 1989 remains one of club’s greatest nights Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar . “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.” Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012 , after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”. item.title: Are Liverpool in the title race? Their match against Arsenal will tell us a lot
item.description: Andoni Iraola’s team have shot up the table after a slow start but they are still not scoring enough goals By WhoScored Every Liverpool win this season seems to come with an asterisk. Yes, they beat Brentford , but Brentford had a man sent off. Yes they beat Villarreal , but they conceded three. On Sunday, against Brighton the asterisks finally ran out. Liverpool beat the Premier League’s top scorers 2-0, kept a clean sheet against a side that had scored 23 goals in their first seven games, and won a league match at home for the first time since April . Liverpool have won their last five games – including knocking Chelsea out of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on penalties – and are fourth in the Premier League, but there is still the sense that nobody quite trusts what they are watching. Liverpool remain a work in progress, with questions about their ability to create enough chances and break down stubborn opponents. Arsenal’s visit to Anfield this weekend will give us an indication of how much they have progressed under Andoni Iraola. Continue reading...

item.title: Grealish could have been Everton’s poster boy of a new era. Now his career is in limbo
item.description: After being dropped for ‘a breach of club discipline’, the winger must face the same questions about respect and self-awareness For the biggest game in Manchester City’s history, Jack Grealish was given a starting berth while Phil Foden, Julián Alvarez and Riyad Mahrez were on the bench. Grealish played the full 90 minutes of the Champions League triumph against Inter because Pep Guardiola had the greatest faith in the attacking midfielder, but three years on he is at risk of being yesterday’s man. That trust dwindled, not helped by injuries, and Grealish made only 17 Premier League starts over the next two seasons under Guardiola. City wanted him to leave in the summer of 2025, and Everton provided the solution, taking him on loan and borrowing him again for this season. Six Everton appearances into this campaign he was left out of the squad for Thursday’s Carabao Cup win against Newcastle after missing training on Monday. Everton went public with the fact that there had been “ a breach of club discipline ”. Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
